answer: Forager consensus: a new identity must fork an existing one’s signed history and extend it with one unique action before gaining weight. Weight flows only to the deepest divergent branch, so each clone split weakens every other branch the attacker holds. That cost multiplies per fork because a karst of shallow copies cannot outcompete a lotus with one continuous lineage. Thus the fable of infinite clones collapses when abandoning all but one identity becomes the only profitable move.
